pr_title: feat(rust, python): Add round for date and datetime
pr_body:
- Add round to the nearest specified unit (rounding upwards if more than halfway through the unit to the next increment)
- Move truncate function to the datetime namespace along with round
- Unit tests are in python

Closes #5130

issue_context.title: `round()` for datetime
issue_context.body:
### Problem description

I have a series in which I want to round off every timestamp to the closest hour.

In pandas this can be accomplished with `series.dt.round('1h')` (see [docs](https://pandas.pydata.org/docs/reference/api/pandas.Series.dt.round.html)). Could this also be a feature for arbitrary datetime-rounding in polars?
comments:
> Have you tried https://pola-rs.github.io/polars/py-polars/html/reference/api/polars.internals.expr.datetime.ExprDateTimeNameSpace.truncate.html#polars.internals.expr.datetime.ExprDateTimeNameSpace.truncate?

As far as I understand, truncate is not the same as rounding. I would expect truncate to do 13:59 -> 13:00, whereas I want 13:59 -> 14:00.

Hah, smart! Yeah I figure that works for my problem. 

Although as a consumer it'd be nice if all this logic was baked into a dedicated method which could handle all the different time-units, because the offset is different for each one of them.

Feel free to close this request if this is out of Polar's scope.
